name: AlphaProof
one_liner: An AlphaZero-style agent learns to prove competition problems in Lean by reinforcement learning and trains on variants of hard problems.

loop.proposes: Lean proofs, built step by step, for millions of auto-formalized problems
loop.judged_by: The Lean proof assistant, which verifies every proof
loop.steers: Verified outcomes train the model; for hard problems, test-time RL learns from millions of related variants

headline_result: At IMO 2024 the system with AlphaProof as its core engine solved three of the five non-geometry problems, including the hardest one; combined with AlphaGeometry 2 this reached a score equivalent to a silver medallist, with multi-day computation.
caveat: Problems were formalized into Lean before the system worked on them, and the paper reports multi-day computation, so this is far from a competition-time-limit result. The Nature paper's claim is the RL method; the medal-level score is the combined system.
beyond_harness_note: Lean's verdicts train the model by reinforcement learning, including at test time on problem variants, and the output is a machine-checked proof.
generative_model: AlphaZero-inspired agent trained on millions of auto-formalized problems

sources.title: Olympiad-level formal mathematical reasoning with reinforcement learning
